extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent agents, attorneys, Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff, and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural requirements for approving an Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and ordering a practitioner's exclusion on consent, plus related obligations (publication, compliance with CFR provisions, reinstatement consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve affidavit and exclude on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, the USPTO Director has the authority to approve Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude Respondent on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory/regulatory authority underpinning approval of an affidavit of resignation and entry of exclusion on consent; it authorizes the Director to accept an affidavit and order exclusion from patent, trademark, and non-patent practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must 'comply[] with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance includes the elements set out elsewhere in the affidavit (free and voluntary consent, awareness of pending complaint and OED opinion, understanding of relevant CFR provisions, and explicit consent to exclusion). The Director will determine if the affidavit meets §11.27(a) before approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent must be freely and voluntarily rendered
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must state and the practitioner must acknowledge that 'His consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A voluntary, uncoerced statement of consent is a prerequisite to approving exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending disciplinary complaint and its allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner must acknowledge awareness that 'there is a disciplinary complaint currently pending against him before a hearing officer' and the nature of the allegations (misconduct while acting in specified roles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiant should acknowledge the pending complaint and the specific factual allegations and context (e.g., acts while President and Executive Director of NAPP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of OED Director's opinion of specific regulatory violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must reflect awareness that the OED Director is of the opinion that the practitioner violated specified provisions of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 10.23 subsections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit should identify the OED's asserted bases for discipline so the practitioner's consent is informed by the alleged rule violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) — disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: OED alleged violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) (proscribing engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct) by 'misappropriating NAPP funds, using NAPP funds and the NAPP credit card for personal use without authorization, submitting false financial reports to NAPP, and/or breaching the fiduciary duties of utmost good faith, loyalty, trust, and confidence' owed to NAPP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given (misappropriation, unauthorized personal use, false reports, breach of fiduciary duties) illustrate conduct that may constitute disreputable or gross misconduct under §10.23(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) — illegal conduct involving moral turpitude
rubrics_metrics.description: OED alleged violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) (proscribing engaging in illegal conduct involving moral turpitude) by reference to violations of Georgia criminal statutes (e.g., theft by taking, theft by deception, theft by conversion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should convey that alleged criminal statutes/acts may amount to conduct involving moral turpitude for disciplinary purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: OED alleged violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) (proscribing engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation) by 'misappropriating NAPP funds, using NAPP funds and the NAPP credit card for personal use without authorization, and/or submitting false financial reports to NAPP that concealed his misconduct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of false financial reports and concealment of misconduct are given as prototypical examples of dishonesty or fraud under §10.23(b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — other conduct adversely reflecting on fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: OED alleged violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) (proscribing engaging in other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO) by 'engaging in the acts and omissions described expressly or impliedly in the pending disciplinary complaint.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subsection serves as a catch‑all for conduct not otherwise enumerated that nonetheless undermines a practitioner's fitness to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of reinstatement presumption under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner must acknowledge that, 'if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (i) the allegations set forth in the disciplinary complaint pending against him are true and (ii) he could not have successfully defended himself against such allegations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a critical collateral consequence of consenting to exclusion: at reinstatement the facts alleged in the dismissed complaint are conclusively presumed true for the limited purpose of the reinstatement decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner must fully read and understand 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must state that he 'has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60, and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of requesting and consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should reflect comprehension of the procedural rules governing resignation/exclusion, client notification/handling, publication, and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner must consent to being excluded from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must include an explicit statement that 'He consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit, affirmative consent to exclusion is required for approval under §11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette (the Notice of Exclusion on Consent containing specified substantive statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published notice should include the practitioner's name and registration number, that the affidavit was accepted, the fact that the affidavit was submitted while a disciplinary complaint was pending, a summary of the OED's opinion regarding rule violations and alleged facts, and the reinstatement-presumption language; decisions are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order states: 'Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 contains practitioner obligations after an adverse action (e.g., client notices, file handling). The practitioner is required to follow those post-exclusion duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order states: 'The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.59 concerns publication and notification duties by the Office; the OED Director must carry out those duties (e.g., publication in Official Gazette and posting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 when seeking reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order states: 'Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, if and when he seeks reinstatement to practice before the Office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the practitioner later seeks reinstatement, he must follow the reinstatement procedures and requirements of §11.60 (and recognize the presumption described in the affidavit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order provides: 'The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No shifting of costs between the OED Director and the respondent for costs incurred to date or in carrying out the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint motion to dismiss pending disciplinary complaint within 14 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall 'jointly move to dismiss the pending disciplinary complaint within fourteen days of the date of this Final Order.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the Director approves the affidavit and orders exclusion on consent, the parties are required to promptly move to dismiss the underlying disciplinary complaint within the specified 14-day timeframe.
